To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alveolar fluid removal by epithelial sodium transporters plays a critical role in the resolution of pulmonary oedemas.

alveolar fluid is reabsorbed by active ion transport across alveolar epithelial cells, that the rate of fluid reabsorption can be upregulated in experimental models of lung injury, and that the mechanisms of upregulation may lead to new therapeutic strategies for the management of pulmonary oedemas.

1) the alveolar type II epithelium has an important role in the resolution of pulmonary oedemas and 2) pharmacologic manipulation of the alveolus epithelium may be an effective strategy for treating pulmonary oedemas.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular and cellular mechanisms of alveolar epithelial ion and fluid transport, the regulation of these processes and their relevance for the development, progression and resolution of alveolar flooding in acute respiratory distress syndrome.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control alveolar fluid balance and how they are altered by injury to the alveolus
the mechanisms that control alveolar epithelial ion transport and fluid clearance in health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the alveolar fluid removal mechanisms are important for the resolution of alveolar pulmonary oedema and that pharmacological interventions to enhance the rate and/or capacity for fluid removal from the distal lung may lead to improved clinical outcomes.

alveolar epithelial sodium transport is a critical determinant of alveolar liquid balance and that impairment of alveolar sodium transport may play a key role in the pathogenesis of pulmonary oedemas.
alveolar oesophageal fluid clearance mechanisms are central to the development of acute lung injury and that therapeutic strategies that target these mechanisms may be beneficial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alveolar epithelial sodium transport is an important mechanism for the resolution of oedema in the lung.
there is a strong need for a better understanding of the mechanisms of alveolar epithelial sodium transport, which may lead to new therapies for pulmonary oedema.

there is a need for a better understanding of the mechanisms of pulmonary oedemagenesis and resolution, and that the development of new therapeutic strategies to treat pulmonary oedema will be facilitated by the identification of the molecular pathways that regulate fluid transport in the distal lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alveolar epithelial ion transport is an important target for the development of novel therapies for acute lung injury and pulmonary oedema.

the molecular mechanisms for alveolar fluid absorption are now better understood and that this information may provide a rational basis for new therapeutic strategies for pulmonary oedema, especially for those types that are associated with acute lung injury.

there is a critical role for alveolar epithelial sodium transporters and sodium pumps in the resolution of alveolar pulmonary oedema, and that pharmacological or genetic interventions that enhance alveolar sodium reabsorption may be a useful approach to the prevention or treatment of pulmonary oedemas.
